premises: In concentrated alloys, lattice thermal conductivity can dominate at low temperatures and become comparable to electronic thermal conductivity near room temperature.
Chemical disorder scatters electrons more effectively than phonons in concentrated alloys.
The cited evidence (E2) is for NiCoFeCrMn and NiCoFeCrPd, not HfNbTaTiZr.
Ab initio methods (E1) can provide elastic constants and Debye temperatures for concentrated alloys.
A multi-scale framework coupling ab initio electronic structure with atomistic phonon calculations will reduce prediction error by ~30% compared to Debye-based models.
